doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Musical family and idolizing brother Abe
summary: His father sang like a cantor; he idolized his much older clarinetist brother and inherited his clarinets.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Was he or your mother musical?

Actually my father was kind of, he used to sing in the temple and things like that, like almost like a cantor, but not officially a cantor. And my mother had a good ear. But they didn’t have any music — they weren’t in any musical things.
So I wonder where those musical genes came from in you and your brother?

We’re not really sure except of course I idolized my brother when I was growing up you know, he was already on the road with Les Brown or Tommy Dorsey and he’s ten or eleven years older, so as I say I idolized him when I was growing up because he was playing these great clarinet solos and everything.
That’s good. A lot of times siblings don’t exactly get along too well.
Right. No I got his old metal clarinet then I got his other clarinet you know, the Selmer.
